items.pronunciation_notes: The ज़्य is a single cluster with the y folded in: zyaa-daa.

learn.title_en: ज़्यादा ends in -ा and never changes
learn.explanation_en: ज़्यादा means more or too much, and although it ends in -ा it is invariable — ज़्यादा पानी and ज़्यादा चाय, with no ज़्यादी anywhere. That puts it with हमेशा among words whose ending promises agreement and does not deliver. It covers both comparison and excess: ज़्यादा दो means give more, ज़्यादा मत बोलो means do not talk too much. Its opposite is कम, less, which is also invariable.

examples.note: A common short answer about quantity.
मत for the negative imperative, from Module 7.
ज़्यादा is unchanged while महँगा agrees, since only the second is marked.

common_error.why_en: ज़्यादा never changes, despite the -ा ending. चाय being feminine makes no difference to it.

practice.question: ज़्यादा
practice.explanation_en: ज़्यादा is more or too much, and it never changes its form.

game.explanation_en: ज़्यादा, unchanged. The -ा ending here is not an agreement ending at all.

items.pronunciation_notes: Aspirated th at the front and a flapped ड़ before the ending: tho-ṛaa.

learn.title_en: थोड़ा agrees where ज़्यादा does not
learn.explanation_en: थोड़ा means a little, and unlike ज़्यादा it is a marked adjective, so it agrees: थोड़ा पानी, थोड़ी चाय, थोड़े लोग. Two words meaning nearly opposite things, both ending in -ा, and only one of them changes. That is the clearest possible demonstration that the ending alone tells you nothing. Used adverbially it stays थोड़ा — थोड़ा तेज़ है, it is a bit spicy — and थोड़ा सा is a softened just a little.

examples.note: पानी is masculine, so थोड़ा.
चाय is feminine, so थोड़ी — where ज़्यादा would not have changed.
Used adverbially here, so it stays थोड़ा.

common_error.why_en: चाय is feminine and थोड़ा is marked, so it agrees. This is exactly where ज़्यादा would not have.

practice.question: थोड़ा
practice.explanation_en: थोड़ा is a little, and unlike ज़्यादा it agrees with the noun.

game.explanation_en: थोड़ी, because चाय is feminine and थोड़ा is a marked adjective.

items.pronunciation_notes: Aspirated ph with a puff of air, not an f: phir, one syllable.

learn.title_en: फिर sequences, and फिर से repeats
learn.explanation_en: फिर means then in the sense of next, and it is how you string events together: पहले यह, फिर वह. With से it becomes फिर से, again or once more, which is what you say when you want something repeated. Two set phrases are worth having whole: फिर मिलेंगे, we will meet again, is the standard way to say goodbye, and फिर भी means even so or nevertheless. Note the aspirated ph — this is not the dotted फ़.

examples.note: फिर से for repetition, using the same से as manner adverbs.
The standard goodbye, in the plural future.
पहले and फिर sequencing two instructions.

common_error.why_en: फिर alone means then or next. For again you need फिर से, or the listener will wait for what comes after.

practice.question: फिर से
practice.explanation_en: फिर से is again. फिर on its own means then or next.

game.question_en: Which phrase is the standard way to say goodbye?
game.explanation_en: फिर मिलेंगे — we will meet again, in the plural future.

summary.recap_en: ज़्यादा and थोड़ा both end in -ा, mean roughly opposite things, and only थोड़ा agrees. That pair is the clearest evidence in the module that an ending on its own predicts nothing — which is what the gender flag has been insisting all along.
summary.next_up_en: Next: the verbs that close the module, starting with the two that do most of the work in Hindi.

items.pronunciation_notes: Short i and no vowel before the न: mil-naa.
items.gloss_en: to meet; to be received, to be available

learn.title_en: One verb, two constructions, two meanings
learn.explanation_en: मिलना does two jobs and the postposition tells you which. With से it means to meet: मैं उससे मिला, I met him. With को it means to be received or obtained: मुझे किताब मिली, I got the book. The second is how Hindi says get anything at all — a job, a discount, a salary, a chance — and you have already seen it with तनख़्वाह and छूट. Crucially मिलना is intransitive, so no ने is ever involved and every tense is open to you.

examples.note: से for meeting a person, and the perfective works since मिलना is intransitive.
को for receiving, and मिली agrees with the feminine किताब.
The habitual, for what a place sells or offers.

common_error.why_en: मिलना is intransitive, so the subject stays plain. ने belongs only to transitive verbs in the perfective.

practice.prompt_en: What does मुझे किताब मिली mean?
practice.question: मुझे किताब मिली
practice.explanation_en: With को, मिलना means to be received. With से it would mean to meet.

game.question_en: Which postposition makes मिलना mean to meet someone?
game.explanation_en: से मिलना is to meet. को मिलना is to receive something.

items.pronunciation_notes: No vowel between the ग and the न: lag-naa.
items.gloss_en: to attach; to seem; to feel; to take time

learn.title_en: The most overworked verb in the language
learn.explanation_en: लगना has appeared in this module more than any other verb — डर लगना, भूख लगना, ठंड लगना, चोट लगना, लाइन में लगना — and its core sense is attaching or taking hold. Two more uses are worth having. मुझे अच्छा लगता है means I like it, literally it feels good to me, and it is more common than पसंद. And समय लगता है means it takes time, which is how Hindi expresses duration. All of them are intransitive, so ने never appears.

examples.note: Literally it feels good to me, with the person marked by को.
लगना for duration — the time attaches to the task.

examples.english: I think, it seems to me
examples.note: The seeming sense, used to soften an opinion.

common_error.why_en: That says you seem nice to someone else. For liking something, the person feeling it takes को.

practice.prompt_en: What does मुझे अच्छा लगता है mean?
practice.question: मुझे अच्छा लगता है
practice.explanation_en: Literally it feels good to me — the ordinary way to say you like something.

game.question_en: Which verb goes with समय for how long something takes?
game.explanation_en: समय लगता है — the time attaches to the task.

items.pronunciation_notes: Two long syllables with nothing between them: laa-naa.

learn.title_en: A transitive verb that takes no ने
learn.explanation_en: लाना means to bring, and it is transitive — you bring something. But it is one of a small handful of transitive verbs that refuse the ने construction anyway: मैं पानी लाया, not मैंने. That is genuinely irregular, and it has a practical consequence right now — the perfective of लाना is available to you when almost no other transitive verb's is. भूलना, to forget, behaves the same way. Module 9 will explain the construction and name the exceptions; these two you can use today.

examples.note: The तुम imperative.
No ने, even though लाना is transitive — this is the exception.
The verb agrees with the subject, which it would not do if ने were involved.

common_error.why_en: लाना never takes ने, so the subject stays plain and the verb agrees with it rather than with the object.

practice.question: लाना
practice.explanation_en: लाना is to bring, and it is a transitive verb that takes no ने.

game.question_en: Which other verb also refuses ने?
game.explanation_en: भूलना, to forget. Both लाना and भूलना are transitive and take no ने.

summary.recap_en: मिलना and लगना are the two hardest-working verbs in Hindi and both are intransitive, so every tense is open to you. लाना is transitive and still takes no ने, which makes its perfective usable a whole module early.
summary.next_up_en: Next: telling, showing and forgetting, and the postpositions each one demands.

items.pronunciation_notes: Three syllables with the length on the second: ba-taa-naa.

learn.title_en: बताना takes को, where पूछना takes से
learn.explanation_en: बताना is to tell, and the person told takes को: मुझे बताओ, tell me. Set it beside पूछना, which takes से — you ask a person से and tell them को. That split has now appeared four times in this module and it is worth trusting: things moving towards a person take को, things drawn out of them take से. बताना is the transitive partner of the long-aa pattern, and it is transitive, so its perfective waits for Module 9.

examples.note: The person told takes को, so मुझे.
सब means everything, and the habitual is safe with a transitive verb.
The polite imperative, and a sentence worth having ready.

common_error.why_en: बताना takes को for the person told. से belongs with पूछना, and the two are easy to swap.

practice.question: बताना
practice.explanation_en: बताना is to tell, and the person told takes को.

game.question_en: Which postposition marks the person you tell?
game.explanation_en: मुझे बताओ — को for telling, से for asking.

items.pronunciation_notes: Aspirated kh in the middle and the length on that syllable: di-khaa-naa.

learn.title_en: दिखाना is देखना with the long aa
learn.explanation_en: देखना is to see and दिखाना is to show — to cause someone to see. That is the long-aa causative pattern again, for the sixth time in this module, and by now it should be predictable rather than surprising. Like बताना, the person shown takes को. दिखाइए is what you say in a shop: यह दिखाइए, show me this one, which is more useful than almost any other sentence when buying something.

examples.note: को for the person shown, exactly as with बताना.
The polite imperative — the shop sentence worth over-learning.

examples.hindi: वह मुझे घर दिखा रहा है
examples.read_as: vah mujhe ghar dikhaa rahaa hai
examples.english: he is showing me the house
examples.note: The continuous, which is safe with any verb.

common_error.why_en: देखना is to see, so मुझे देखो means look at me. To be shown something you need the causative दिखाना.

practice.question: दिखाना
practice.explanation_en: दिखाना is to show — देखना with the long aa inserted.

game.question_en: Which verb is दिखाना built from?
game.explanation_en: देखना, to see. Inserting a long aa makes it causative — to make someone see.

tts_strings: वह मुझे घर दिखा रहा है

items.pronunciation_notes: Breathy bh and a long uu, with no vowel before the न: bhuul-naa.

learn.title_en: The second verb that refuses ने
learn.explanation_en: भूलना is to forget, and like लाना it is transitive and still takes no ने: मैं भूल गया, I forgot. So its perfective is available to you now, which matters because forgetting is something you mostly report in the past. It is the opposite of याद रखना from level twenty-six, and the pair is worth holding together: याद रखो and मत भूलो say the same thing from two directions.

examples.note: No ने, and the verb agrees with the subject.
मत for the negative imperative.
Feminine agreement on the subject, which ने would have blocked.

common_error.why_en: भूलना takes no ने, so the subject stays plain — one of only a handful of transitive verbs that behave this way.

practice.question: भूलना
practice.explanation_en: भूलना is to forget, and it is the second transitive verb that takes no ने.

game.question_en: Which phrase means the opposite of मत भूलो?
game.explanation_en: याद रखो — keep it in mind, which is मत भूलो from the other direction.

summary.recap_en: बताना and दिखाना both take को for the person, where पूछना takes से — things moving towards a person take को, things drawn out of them take से. दिखाना is देखना with the long aa, which is the sixth causative pair in this module.
summary.next_up_en: Next: thinking, wanting and stopping — three verbs you will need to say what you intend.

items.pronunciation_notes: Long open o and no vowel before the न: soch-naa.

learn.explanation_en: सोचना is to think in the sense of considering or working something out, and what you think about takes के बारे में: इसके बारे में सोचो, think about it. That is different from मुझे लगता है, which means I think in the sense of an opinion or impression. English uses think for both; Hindi separates deliberate thought from a passing view, and using सोचना for an opinion sounds oddly heavy.

examples.note: The continuous, for thought in progress.
के बारे में for the subject of thought.
लगना for an opinion, rather than सोचना.

common_error.wrong: मैं सोचता हूँ कि यह अच्छा है
common_error.right: मुझे लगता है कि यह अच्छा है
common_error.why_en: For an opinion Hindi prefers लगना. सोचना suggests you have been deliberating about it.

practice.question: सोचना
practice.explanation_en: सोचना is deliberate thinking. For an opinion, Hindi uses लगना instead.

game.question_en: Which phrase marks what you are thinking about?
game.explanation_en: के बारे में — about. इसके बारे में सोचो, think about it.

items.pronunciation_notes: The ह is a breath between the vowel and the न: chaah-naa.

learn.title_en: चाहना takes a bare infinitive in front of it
learn.explanation_en: चाहना is to want, and when you want to do something the verb goes in front of it as a plain infinitive: मैं जाना चाहता हूँ, I want to go. Nothing comes between them and no को is needed. Compare चाहिए, which you met with मुझे मदद चाहिए — that is a different construction meaning need, and it takes को for the person. So चाहना is wanting and चाहिए is needing, and they are built completely differently.

examples.note: The infinitive जाना sits directly in front of चाहना.

examples.english: what do you want to do?
examples.note: तुम takes plural agreement on both verbs.
चाहिए for needing, with the person marked by को.

common_error.why_en: चाहिए is a fixed form meaning need and takes को. For wanting, चाहना conjugates normally.

practice.question: चाहना
practice.explanation_en: चाहना is to want. चाहिए is a different construction meaning need.

game.question_en: What form does the verb take in front of चाहना?
game.explanation_en: The plain infinitive — जाना चाहता हूँ, करना चाहते हो.

items.pronunciation_notes: Short u and no vowel before the न: ruk-naa.
items.gloss_en: to stop, to wait, to stay

learn.title_en: रुकना covers stopping, waiting and staying
learn.explanation_en: रुकना is intransitive and means to come to a stop, which stretches to waiting and to staying somewhere overnight. रुको on its own is the ordinary way to say wait. Its transitive partner is रोकना, to stop something — and note the vowel change rather than a long aa, which is a second causative pattern worth knowing: रुकना to रोकना, उठना to उठाना, बनना to बनाना. Since रुकना is intransitive, every tense is open.

examples.note: The तुम imperative, and the most common use of the verb.
रुकी agrees with the feminine गाड़ी, and the perfective works.
रोकना is the transitive partner — you are stopping it.

common_error.why_en: रुकना means to stop by itself. To stop something else you need the transitive रोकना.

practice.question: रुकना
practice.explanation_en: रुकना is to stop or wait, and it is intransitive.

game.question_en: Which form do you use to stop a vehicle?
game.explanation_en: रोकना — the transitive partner, formed by a vowel change rather than a long aa.

summary.recap_en: सोचना is deliberate thinking while लगना carries an opinion, and Hindi keeps them apart where English uses think for both. चाहना takes a bare infinitive in front of it, and रुकना introduces a second causative pattern — a vowel change rather than a long aa.
summary.next_up_en: Next: the last two verbs, and a conversation that closes the module.

items.pronunciation_notes: Aspirated kh with a puff of air and a long open o: khol-naa.
items.gloss_en: to open, to undo, to untie

learn.explanation_en: खोलना is to open, and it covers doors, windows, bottles, knots, shoelaces and bank accounts — anything that goes from closed to open. Its intransitive partner is खुलना, to open by itself: दरवाज़ा खुला, the door opened. That is the vowel-change causative again, the same pattern as रुकना and रोकना. खोलना is transitive, so its perfective waits for Module 9, but the imperative and the present are yours.

examples.note: The तुम imperative — खोलना is transitive.
खुलना is intransitive, and खुलती agrees with the feminine दुकान.
बंद is the adjective for closed, and it never changes.

common_error.why_en: The shop opens by itself, so the intransitive खुलना. खोलना would need someone doing the opening.

practice.question: खोलना
practice.explanation_en: खोलना is to open something. खुलना is for something opening by itself.

game.question_en: Which form do you use when a shop opens by itself?
game.explanation_en: खुलना — the intransitive partner, formed by a vowel change.

items.pronunciation_notes: Long uu and an aspirated chh with no vowel before the न: puuchh-naa.

learn.title_en: पूछना closes the से and को pair
learn.explanation_en: पूछना is to ask, and the person asked takes से — मुझसे पूछो, ask me. It has turned up in this module with सवाल, रास्ता, टीचर, दुकानदार and पड़ोसी, always with से, and it is the counterpart of बताना, which always takes को. That single split covers a great deal of Hindi: information drawn out of a person uses से, information given to a person uses को. Between them, पूछना and बताना are most of what a conversation is made of.

examples.note: से for the person asked, where बताना would take को.
The person takes से and the thing asked about is the object.
मत for the negative imperative, from Module 7.

common_error.why_en: पूछना takes से. मुझे would be the को form, which belongs with बताना and देना.

practice.question: पूछना
practice.explanation_en: पूछना is to ask, and the person asked always takes से.

game.question_en: Which pair of postpositions is correct?
game.explanation_en: पूछना से, बताना को — drawn out of a person uses से, given to them uses को.

items.pronunciation_notes: The three words run together, with the plural ending clear on आए: aa-e haiṁ.

learn.title_en: Four lines, and everything in them is from this module
learn.explanation_en: This closes Module 8, so it is worth noticing what the exchange is built from. खोलो and खोलता हूँ are from this level, मेहमान from the relationships block, क्या हुआ from Module 7, and आए हैं is the perfective present of an intransitive verb, which needs no ने. Nothing here is beyond what you now have. That is the point of a vocabulary module placed in the middle of the course rather than at the start: the grammar was already in place, so the words could go straight to work.

lines.speaker: B
lines.hindi: ठीक है, मैं अभी खोलता हूँ।
lines.read_as: ṭhiik hai, maiṁ abhii kholtaa huuṁ.
lines.english: All right, I will open it now.

common_error.why_en: Guests take plural agreement, both for number and as a mark of respect.

practice.question: मेहमान आए हैं
practice.explanation_en: The perfective present — they have arrived and are here now.

game.question_en: Listen to the third line. Which word is missing?
game.explanation_en: मेहमान takes plural agreement, so the perfective participle is आए.

tts_strings: ठीक है, मैं अभी खोलता हूँ।

summary.recap_en: Module 8 is complete at 165 words. Two things are worth carrying forward above the vocabulary itself. First, the collocation is part of the word — काम करना, बारिश होना, डर लगना, परीक्षा देना — and no rule predicts it. Second, causative pairs are everywhere: insert a long aa or change the vowel, and an intransitive verb becomes the version where someone is doing it.
summary.next_up_en: Next is Module 9 and the ने construction — the one piece of grammar this entire module has been working around, and the reason so many perfectives have been off limits.
